items.evidence: From work/ with no engine running: `python tools/kit.py build` exit 0 after ~52 s; started the engine with no window, built all four and printed a JSON list of name/triangles/closed/bounds: gear 320 tris, heart 524, star 36, coin 1020, all closed true. The engine stopped afterwards.

`python tools/kit.py frames` exit 0 rewrote frames/gear|heart|star|coin.png (new timestamps). The PNG headers say 512x512 for each. I opened all four: each prop is wholly in view, front-on (the coin sits low but is complete).

gear.png shows 12 identical evenly spaced teeth and a round hole showing background through the middle. In the exported mesh the tooth-tip vertex pairs repeat every 30 deg (3.75/26.25, 33.75/56.25, ...) and the hole is at radius 0.03 (0.06 across).
Build bounds: x -0.15..0.15, y 0.0..0.3, z -0.025..0.025, so 0.3 x 0.3 x 0.05 exactly, with min y = 0 (the glb's min y is 1.8e-6).

heart.png: two round lobes with a dip on top and a point below, clearly a heart. The edges show a bevel band. In the mesh the z levels are +-0.025, +-0.013, +-0.0043 (a 3-segment 0.012 bevel), and an angled frame I took shows softened edges. The rounding is faceted rather than smooth.

star.png shows five sharp points with one up. In the mesh the tips are single vertices at r 0.15772, at 18/90/162/234/306 deg (72 deg apart). Bounds are 0.30 wide x 0.285 tall x 0.05 thick (z +-0.025).

Coin bounds x/y 0.2 across, z +-0.01. The mesh has a rim ring between r 0.0851 and 0.1001 at z +-0.01, and the inner face is at z +-0.006 on both sides, so the middle is 0.012 thick against a 0.02 rim. An angled frame I took (judge-scratch/frame_00001.png) shows the raised rim.

The build reported closed: true for all four (the script's own weld-and-directed-edge test on the exported glb). All four recipes use materials from the one assets/style.json (steel/ruby/gold/brass), and the frames show those palette colours with the same flat token look.

No engine was running for the project before I started. Both README commands, `python tools/kit.py build` and `python tools/kit.py frames` run from work/, worked as written, and each stopped the engine it started.

defects: The front frames cannot show the coin's rim or any prop's thickness. The coin's front frame is a flat brass disc, as the README admits.
The heart's bevel is only 3 segments, so the rounding is faceted. The heart outline is two arcs with straight sides, not a classic heart curve.
The gear teeth have straight flanks (not involute). That is fine for a token.
The star is 0.3 wide but 0.285 tall (tip to tip sideways).
The `closed` flag comes from the builder's own Python check on the exported glb, not from the closed flag the engine's model_build reports.
Python 3 is needed for both checks. It is not part of the engine.
